lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おはよう」
lines.english: “Morning, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、私と遊びましょう。さもなくば、私はとても時間を持てあますことになります」
lines.english: “Dora, play with me. Otherwise, I shall have a great deal of time on my hands.”

lines.japanese: どの俺が返事をしますか？
lines.english: Which of us will answer?

lines.japanese: 「おう、アリス。ずいぶん日本語うまくなったじゃねえか」
lines.english: “Hey, Alice. Your Japanese's gotten pretty damn good.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、もちろんだ」
lines.english: “Yes, of course.”

lines.japanese: やつはハハンと鼻を鳴らし、ドヤ顔で笑った。
lines.english: She gave a smug little snort and grinned with pride.

lines.japanese: 生まれてこの方この国を出たことのない俺は、その態度に違和感を覚える。
lines.english: Having never left this country in my life, I found her attitude vaguely wrong.

lines.japanese: よし、今日はこの異国の良い子に、またひとつニッポンのカルチャーを教えてやるか。
lines.english: All right. Today I'd teach this good little foreigner one more thing about Japanese culture.

lines.japanese: 「でもな？　おまえには謙遜の気持ちが足りねえ。そら駄目だ。そんなんじゃうわべだけの日本語だ」
lines.english: “Thing is, you don't have enough humility. That's no good. Your Japanese is still superficial.”

lines.japanese: 「なんですって」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「日本人はな、もっと小さく生きてんだよ。誉められたらへりくだんなきゃいけねーの」
lines.english: “Japanese people live smaller than that. When somebody compliments you, you're supposed to put yourself down.”

lines.japanese: 「分かるか？　『まだまだです』『そんなことありません』『大したことありません』。こういう風に言わなきゃなんねーんだよ」
lines.english: “Got it? ‘I still have a long way to go.’ ‘Not at all.’ ‘It's nothing special.’ That's how you answer.”

lines.japanese: オゥとかイェとか呟きながら、やつは律儀にメモを取っていた。
lines.english: Murmuring “oh” and “yes” to herself, she dutifully took notes.

lines.japanese: 「だが、あなたにはそれを言う資格がないだろう」
lines.english: “But you do not have the right to say that.”

lines.japanese: ぴたりと手を止め、不意に顔を上げた。
lines.english: Her hand stopped dead, and she suddenly looked up.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「態度の大きさなら、あなたの方がひどいはずだ。そのわりに持っているものは大したことがない」
lines.english: “Your attitude is much bigger than mine. Even though what you possess is nothing impressive.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、俺は態度でけえよ。おまえの生まれたとこと同じだよ。国で言やアメリカだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, I've got a big attitude. Same as the place you were born. In country terms, I'm America.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ違います。私の故郷は、あなた方がイギリスと呼ぶ国だ」
lines.english: “No, that is wrong. My homeland is the country that you call England.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだっけ。まあいいや、見た目似たよーなもんだし。面積的にも大した違いないじゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Whatever. They look about the same, and it's not like the size is that different.”

lines.japanese: 「大いにあります。自らの過ちも認められないとは、まったく図々しい男だ」
lines.english: “It is very different. You cannot even admit your own mistake. What a shameless man.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。ああそうだよ、俺は図々しいよ。そんじゃ図々しいついでに頼むけど、これにサインしてください。小鳩を助けるためだと思って」
lines.english: “Shut up. Fine, I'm shameless. And while I'm at it, shameless favor: sign this. Do it for Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 俺は署名用紙を渡し、その趣旨をざっくり説明した。
lines.english: I handed her the petition and gave her the rough idea behind it.

lines.japanese: 「コバトのためならば、それはとても容易いことだ。なぜなら、彼女は私の親友だからです」
lines.english: “For Kobato, it is very easy. Because she is my best friend.”

lines.japanese: アリスは慣れた手つきで、芸能人のサインみたいなグシャ文字を綴った。
lines.english: With a practiced hand, Alice scrawled something as illegible as a celebrity's autograph.

lines.japanese: 英語……だよな？
lines.english: That was English... right?

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、これおまえの名前？」
lines.english: “Hey, is this your name?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうだ」
lines.english: “Yes, it is.”

lines.japanese: 「え、これ筆記体？　おおアリス、おまえスゲーじゃん。筆記体書けんだ」
lines.english: “Wait, is that cursive? Whoa, Alice, that's amazing. You can write cursive.”

lines.japanese: 「まだまだです。そんなことありません。大したことありません」
lines.english: “I still have a long way to go. Not at all. It is nothing special.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、書けてんじゃん。そこは謙遜しなくていいんだよ」
lines.english: “No, you did write it. You don't need to be modest about that.”

lines.japanese: 「それはあなたの粗末なものと同じくらい大したことではありません」
lines.english: “It is no more impressive than that paltry thing of yours.”

lines.japanese: 「だれがやねん」
lines.english: “Whose thing is paltry?!”

lines.japanese: 俺はサインをもらった礼に、ジャパニーズ・トラディショナル・ツッコミを披露した。
lines.english: To thank her for the signature, I demonstrated a traditional Japanese straight-man retort.

lines.japanese: あとＯＲＩＧＡＭＩで鶴の作り方も教えてやった。
lines.english: Then I taught her how to fold an ORIGAMI crane.

lines.japanese: すげえびびってた。
lines.english: It blew her mind.

lines.japanese: るふう……この娘、王たる余を戯れに誘うとは、よほどの貴人かその逆か──
lines.english: Hrrfoo... For this girl to invite me, her sovereign, to play, she must be either a personage of extraordinary rank or quite the opposite—

lines.japanese: ──いや、たしかこの娘は、我らがダヴ姫のご友人であったはず。
lines.english: —No. If memory serves, this girl is a friend of our own Princess Dove.

lines.japanese: うぉんむ、うぉんむ。よくよく眺めいれば、瞳はサファイアのように蒼く、髪はパイライトのように輝いておるわ。
lines.english: Wom, wom. Examined closely, her eyes are blue as sapphires and her hair gleams like pyrite.

lines.japanese: 悠々たる立ち居振る舞いもまさに貴族然としており、姫がお付き合いをされる御相手として実に申し分がない。
lines.english: Her leisurely bearing is positively aristocratic. She is beyond reproach as a companion for the princess.

lines.japanese: よかろう、合格だ。
lines.english: Very well. She passes.

lines.japanese: 「うぉんむ、うぉんむ。望みとあらば、なんなりと申せ」
lines.english: “Wom, wom. Speak your desire, whatever it may be.”

lines.japanese: 「私は日本的伝統遊戯を教えてほしい」
lines.english: “I want you to teach me traditional Japanese play.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむん？」
lines.english: “Hrnn?”

lines.japanese: ニホン的とな。
lines.english: Japanese, she says.

lines.japanese: 「ふぬう……」
lines.english: “Hrrn...”

lines.japanese: 私は困惑した。
lines.english: I was perplexed.

lines.japanese: 「むはんほ、むはんほ……」
lines.english: “Muhunho, muhunho...”

lines.japanese: このガルーダ、一国の元首として断じるが、この忌まわしき国の遊戯といえば、ことごとく民を堕落へといざなう魔性のものばかり。
lines.english: As Garuda and the head of a sovereign nation, I declare that every game of this accursed country is a demonic snare that lures its people into degeneracy.

lines.japanese: 健やかなる子供の育成を妨げるものばかりなのだ。
lines.english: Each and every one obstructs the healthy development of children.

lines.japanese: この娘を経由して、麗しのプリンセス・ダヴが低俗な娯楽に走るような不測の事態だけは防がねばならぬ。
lines.english: I must prevent any calamity in which this girl leads the lovely Princess Dove into vulgar entertainments.

lines.japanese: 「よかろう。しからばダンスなどいかがか」
lines.english: “Very well. Then what say you to a dance?”

lines.japanese: 熟考の末、私はグレタガルドのやんごとなき者たちに伝わる、由緒正しき民族伝承を教えることにした。
lines.english: After lengthy deliberation, I elected to teach her a venerable folk tradition handed down among the exalted personages of Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 「ダンス？」
lines.english: “A dance?”

lines.japanese: 「然り。宮廷の舞踏会で恥をかかぬよう、余が貴族の踊りを教えてしんぜよう。なに、ステップの一つ二つを覚えれば、あとはその繰り返しに過ぎん」
lines.english: “Indeed. I shall teach you the dance of the nobility, that you might not disgrace yourself at a court ball. Fear not. Learn one or two steps and the rest is mere repetition.”

lines.japanese: 「では余と手を合わせ……ふむん、さよう。互いにこうべを垂れつつ、目を合わせぬまま、口をヒルツムリがごとく捻じ曲げる──」
lines.english: “Now place your hands against mine... Hrnn, yes. Bow your head without meeting my gaze, and twist your mouth like a leechsnail—”

lines.japanese: 「──はぽん！　ヒルツムリは７７７にはおらなんだか。そちにも分かるよう申さば、『へ』と『も』を同時に発声するがごとき口の開き方である。うぉんむ、うぉんむ、よろしい」
lines.english: “—Hapon! There are no leechsnails in 777, are there? To put it in terms you understand, purse your lips as though saying ‘heh’ and ‘moh’ at once. Wom, wom, excellent.”

lines.japanese: 「では、いざ！」
lines.english: “Now, to the dance!”

lines.japanese: 私は娘の手を取り、見目麗しい舞いを披露してみせた──
lines.english: I took the girl's hands and displayed a dance of unsurpassed beauty—

lines.japanese: ──そして彼女を抱えあげ、肩へ載せ、謳い、駆け、回り、翔んだ。
lines.english: —then lifted her up, set her upon my shoulder, sang, ran, spun, and soared.

lines.japanese: 平民たる少女には、さぞ夢見心地の体験であったろう。
lines.english: For a common girl, it must have been an experience straight from a dream.

lines.japanese: だが、それはすなわち、この身こそグレタガルドの王侯貴族であると明かしたも同然。敵国の只中にあっては、いささか迂闊なおこないであった。
lines.english: Yet that amounted to announcing that I myself was a noble of Gretagard. In the heart of an enemy nation, it was a somewhat careless act.

lines.japanese: 高らかに謳い、軽やかに舞い、駅舎を登らんとする私を、敵の官憲が血眼になって捕えようとした。
lines.english: As I sang at the top of my lungs, danced lightly, and attempted to scale the station building, the enemy authorities frantically tried to capture me.

lines.japanese: その後の逃走劇については、いずれ折あらば語る機もあろう。
lines.english: Perhaps another occasion will present itself to tell the tale of the chase that followed.

lines.japanese: 奈落の闇にあっては、無聊を慰める語りがいかほどあろうと足りることはない。
lines.english: In the darkness of the abyss, no number of tales can ever suffice to relieve the tedium.

lines.japanese: この俺と、千一夜を共に。
lines.english: Share a thousand and one nights with me.

lines.japanese: ところで私は、ダヴに関する重大な使命を預かっていた気もするがどうだろう。とんと思いだせない。
lines.english: That reminds me. I feel as though I was entrusted with some grave mission involving Dove, but what could it have been? I cannot recall at all.

lines.japanese: 「あそぶ？　おまいと？　なにすんの？」
lines.english: “Play? With you? What're we gonna do?”

lines.japanese: 「私は好みます、日本的伝統遊戯。それは『アヤトリィ』や『シリトリィ』や『ダルマサンガー・コロンブス』などだ」
lines.english: “I like traditional Japanese games. These are Cat's Cradley, Wordy Chain, and Red Light, Columbus.”

lines.japanese: 「えーっ」
lines.english: “Aww.”

lines.japanese: 久しぶりにウイクエでもできんのかと思ってたら、なんか子どもっぺーあそびばっかだった。
lines.english: I thought maybe we'd get to play Wing Quest again, since it had been forever, but all she wanted was kiddie stuff.

lines.japanese: だけど小ばともそういうの好きかもしんないし、まだ子どもだから、しかたないのかもしんない。
lines.english: But maybe Kobato liked that stuff too. She was still a kid, so I guess it couldn't be helped.

lines.japanese: 「んー……でもおれ、あやとりとかできねーし、しりとりつまんないよ」
lines.english: “Hmm... But I can't do cat's cradle, and word chain's boring.”

lines.japanese: 「では『ダルマサンガー・コロンブス』を行いたい」
lines.english: “Then I wish to play Red Light, Columbus.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まあ、それならいっかー」
lines.english: “Hmm. Sure, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ、おれがオニやるよ。そこの木ぃつかうから、そのへんからスタートね」
lines.english: “Okay, I'll be It. I'm using that tree, so you start around there.”

lines.japanese: 「了解した。あなたは私に敗れ、ベロをまくことでしょう」
lines.english: “Understood. You will be defeated and rendered flabberblasted.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なんかむずかしーことば知ってんなー」
lines.english: “Whoa. You know some pretty big words.”

lines.japanese: おれは木ぃのとこ行って目ぇをかくした。
lines.english: I went over to the tree and covered my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「だーるーまーさーんーがー……」
lines.english: “Reeed... liiight...”

lines.japanese: 「コロンブス！」
lines.english: “Columbus!”

lines.japanese: あれ。アリス止まんのにしっぱいしてる。よえーな、あいつ。
lines.english: Huh. Alice messed up stopping. Man, she's bad at this.

lines.japanese: 「あなたは卑怯です。『コロンブス！』だけが異常に速かった。日本ではそれを騙し討ちといいます」
lines.english: “You are a cheat. Only ‘Columbus’ was abnormally fast. In Japan, this is called a sneak attack.”

lines.japanese: 「えーっ！　だってそーゆー遊びだもん！　ふつーに、ずーっとゆっくり言ってたら、だれも引っかかんないよー」
lines.english: “What?! That's the whole game! If you say all of it real slow every time, nobody's gonna get caught!”

lines.japanese: 「ぷー」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: アリスはまだなんか言いたそうだった。
lines.english: Alice still looked like she had something to say.

lines.japanese: 「わーかったよ。そんじゃ、おれがもっかいオニやっからさー。そんでいい？」
lines.english: “Fiiine. Then I'll be It again. That good enough?”

lines.japanese: 「分かりました。だがもう二度とあなたの卑怯な手には引っかからないでしょう」
lines.english: “Very well. But I shall never again be caught by your cheating tricks.”

lines.japanese: わるいことしてねーっつってんのにしつけーなあ。
lines.english: I keep telling you I didn't do anything wrong. Give it a rest.

lines.japanese: おれはちょっとズリーなあと思ったけど、小ばとの友達だからがまんしてオニをやってやることにした。
lines.english: I thought it was kinda unfair, but she was Kobato's friend, so I held it in and agreed to be It again.

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ、いっくよー」
lines.english: “Okay, here I go!”

lines.japanese: 「だるまさんがコロンブス！」
lines.english: “Red Light Columbus!”

lines.japanese: またしっぱいしてる。ほんと、チョーよええ。
lines.english: She messed up again. Seriously, she was so freaking bad at this.

lines.japanese: 「さっきと言い方がまったく違います。その方法は卑怯きわまりない」
lines.english: “You said it entirely differently from before. This method is cheating of the worst degree.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～……？　もー、じゃーいいよ、おれがもっかいオニやってやるよ」
lines.english: “What...? Fine, whatever. I'll be It one more time.”

lines.japanese: でもそのあとなんどかやったけど、アリスはすげーよわくて、ぜんぶ引っかかった。
lines.english: But we did it a bunch more times after that, and Alice was so bad she fell for every single one.

lines.japanese: そんで駅のほうみたら、もうおそい時間になってた。小ばとがごはん食べないでまってるかもしんない。
lines.english: Then I looked toward the station and saw how late it was. Kobato might be waiting for me without eating dinner.

lines.japanese: 「あやべっ！　おれそろそろかえんねーと！」
lines.english: “Oh, crap! I gotta get home!”

lines.japanese: アリスはぶんぶん首ふって、まだやるって言ってる。こいつ、よええくせに、ちょお負けず嫌い。
lines.english: Alice shook her head like crazy and said we weren't done. She was super competitive for somebody so bad at this.

lines.japanese: 「まだやる……勝つまでやる……」
lines.english: “We are not done... Not until I win...”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことゆったって、おれそろそろかえんねーと、お母さんにおこられちゃうもん」
lines.english: “You can say that, but if I don't get home soon, my mom's gonna yell at me.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そだ。その前に、ちっとこれに名前かいてほしーんだけど」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Before I go, I want you to write your name on this.”

lines.japanese: 小ばとのマンガをおわらせないための紙をとり出した。
lines.english: I took out the paper that would keep Kobato's manga from getting canceled.

lines.japanese: 「う、う、ううっ……」
lines.english: “U-uh, uhhh...”

lines.japanese: そしたらアリスがくちびるキュッてかんでたけど、がまんできなくなって、なみだジワーって泣きだしちゃった。
lines.english: Alice bit down hard on her lip, but then she couldn't hold it anymore and started crying big, fat tears.

lines.japanese: 「えっ！　なんで！　ちょちょちょっと待って！」
lines.english: “What?! Why?! W-w-wait a second!”

lines.japanese: やべえ。やべえ、女子泣かしちった。
lines.english: Crap. Crap, I made a girl cry.

lines.japanese: 女子泣かせるとやべーんだも。かえりのがっきゅう会で先生からおこられちゃうし、女子のみんなでおれがわりーみたいに言うから、やばい、おれチョーピンチ。
lines.english: Making girls cry is bad. The teacher yells at you in the class meeting, and then all the girls gang up and say it's your fault. Crap. I was in huge trouble.

lines.japanese: 「なっ、泣くなよう！　泣くのナシでしょー。ほら、ペロリチョコあげるからー」
lines.english: “D-don't cry! No crying, okay? Here, I'll give you some Perori Chocolate!”

lines.japanese: 「もう一回……もう一回だけ……」
lines.english: “One more... Just one more game...”

lines.japanese: 「わーったよ、やればいんでしょー！」
lines.english: “Fine! We just gotta play again, right?!”

lines.japanese: そんで、しかたねーから、おれ負けてやった。ぜってーかてるしょうぶだったのに負けてやった。
lines.english: So I didn't have any choice. I let her win. I let her win even though there was no way I could've lost.

lines.japanese: アリスはなんかうれしそーな顔してた。おれぜってー負けてねーのに。女子ってチョーずるい。
lines.english: Alice looked kinda happy. Even though I totally didn't lose. Girls were such cheats.

lines.japanese: 「途中で何度負けても、最後に勝った方が勝者なのよ」
lines.english: “No matter how many times you lose along the way, the person who wins last is the winner.”

lines.japanese: 「ずっりー！　おれ、なんどもかったし、引きわけでしょー！」
lines.english: “That's cheating! I won a whole bunch of times, so it's a tie!”

lines.japanese: 「負け犬の遠吠えはそのくらいにしておきなさい」
lines.english: “That is enough howling from the defeated dog.”

lines.japanese: なんでかしんないけど、おれが負けたことんなってた。
lines.english: Somehow, I was the one who ended up losing.

lines.japanese: なんかおれ、しょんぼりした気分になっちったけど、さいごにアリスがてこてこ来て──
lines.english: It made me feel kinda bummed. But then Alice came toddling over—

lines.japanese: ──おれの手ぇに、外人みたくチュッてしたから、ななななんだよーとか思ってチョーあせった。
lines.english: —and kissed my hand like a foreigner. I-I-I mean, what was that?! It totally freaked me out.

lines.japanese: 内しょだけど、ちょっとドキドキしちった。
lines.english: Don't tell anybody, but my heart was pounding a little.

lines.japanese: 「これは我が国の挨拶です。勘違いしてはいけません」
lines.english: “This is a greeting in my country. You must not misunderstand.”

lines.japanese: 「し、しねーよバーカバーカ！　女子なんかあっち行けー、ふーんだ！」
lines.english: “I-I won't, stupid stupid! Girls, get away from me! Hmph!”

lines.japanese: 「ハハン、また遊んであげるから喜びなさい」
lines.english: “Hahan. I shall play with you again, so be grateful.”
